Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking this RFP. Attached is Dataspan's dedicated capacity questionnaire focused on GPU mix, throughput targets, and reservation planning. Our platform has three primary workload classes:

- Feature store & embeddings (high QPS, small context)
- Real-time chat/generation (low latency, variable context up to 2k tokens)
- Batch analytics / reranking (high throughput, large context up to 8k tokens)

We need a recommended mapping to GPU classes, slab commitment guidance (minimum sustained reserve + burst headroom), and any notes about quantization/throughput trade-offs. Also include target SLOs (p50/p95/p99 token latency) assumptions used to size GPUs.

Attached: dataspan_rfp_questionnaire.xlsx (worksheet: workload_profiles)

Nora — thanks for the questionnaire, received and reviewed. I put together an initial GPU band mapping and a slab sizing proposal (high level) attached as an editable workbook (redwood_gpu_banding_v1.xlsx). Key points up front:

Summary mapping (short):
- Embeddings/feature-store band:
  * Target: 5k+ QPS (batching allowed), median request 16 tokens
  * Recommended GPU class: L4x2 per slab (mixed inference-optimized instances) or A10g for denser packing
  * Slab guidance: Start with 4 slabs => equivalent to ~16 L4 GPUs (sustained 60% util target), burst headroom 2.5x for short windows

- Real-time chat/generation band (1–2k token contexts):
  * Target: p50 token latency <= 15 ms, p95 token latency <= 40 ms, p99 <= 120 ms
  * Recommended GPU class: H100-80GB for latency-critical sessions (model variants up to 70B); A100-80GB for standard gen models
  * Slab guidance: For expected steady traffic (avg 80 concurrent streams), recommend 8 H100-equivalent slabs (each slab = 4 H100 GPUs for isolation) with burst pool of 2 slabs

- Batch analytics / reranking band (8k contexts, high throughput):
  * Target: throughput-oriented — aim for token throughput > 1.2M tokens/s across pool
  * Recommended GPU class: A100-80GB (quantized int8 where acceptable) or H100 for dense large-model offloads
  * Slab guidance: 6 slabs A100-equivalent with auto-scale headroom for nightly peaks

Sizing assumptions and notes:
- "Slab" definition: a logical reserved unit that maps to a small fleet slice (we propose 4 physical GPUs per slab by default for isolation and predictable tail latency). Slab count x GPUs = reserved capacity.
- Utilization target: size for ~55–70% sustained utilization to preserve headroom for tail latency and batch variance.
- Burst policy: allow short burst to 2–3x sustained for <= 15 min, with pre-warmed spare slabs for 1–2 min microbursts.
- Quantization: embeddings and many reranking models can move to int8/4 with minimal accuracy loss; latency-critical generation should start fp16 or bfloat16, move to mixed precision only after eval.

Open clarifying questions (please confirm):
1) Do you require hard isolation (no co-tenancy) across customer datasets for compliance?
2) Expected QPS shape by hour (example: 9am–11am 45% of daily requests?)
3) Any strict tail-latency SLOs beyond p99 token-level metrics?

Attachment: redwood_gpu_banding_v1.xlsx (tab: band_mapping, slab_workbook)

I'll loop in Karthik and Ben for finer throughput math and edge-case packing. If you can share anticipated daily QPS curve and model families (Llama2-70B, Mistral-7B, etc.), we'll refine the slab counts and GPU mix.

Best,

Grace — quick clarifications on a couple of items:

1) Isolation: we require logical isolation per product line (no shared datasets in memory), but physical co-tenancy of GPUs is acceptable if isolation is enforced by containerization and per-tenant KV caches.
2) Burst tolerance: peak windows are often unpredictable — we'd like to allow 3x sustained for at least one 30-minute window/day and microbursts of 5x for <120s.
3) Model families: customers will use a mix — embeddings (openai/embedding-ada-like smaller models), mid-size chat (Mistral/LLama-2-13B), and a small percentage (approx 10%) of 70B variants for high-fidelity synths.

Also curious about the cost delta you expect between A100 and H100 slabs and any recommended split for 70B -> H100 fallback. Can you include an example conversion (slabs -> monthly committed GPUs -> expected token/hour capacity)?

Thanks,
Ethan
Senior Product Ops
Dataspan AI

Nora / Ethan — thanks for the clarifications. We've finalized a conservative-first slab mix and included a conversion workbook attached. Highlights below and attached workbook (slab_commitment_workbook_20280601.xlsx):

Conservative slab proposal (initial commit):
- Bronze (embeddings/feature-store): 6 slabs (24 L4 GPUs equivalent)
  * Sustained capacity: ~6k QPS embeddings (batching median 16 tokens)
  * Burst pool: 2 slabs reserved (pre-warmed), microburst to 5x for short spikes

- Silver (mid-gen / mixed workloads): 10 slabs (40 A100-equivalent GPUs)
  * Sustained: supports ~120 concurrent generation streams at p95 latency targets
  * Burst: allow up to 3x sustained for 30m/day via burst credits; we recommend 2 pre-warmed slabs for <2min bursts

- Gold (70B, high fidelity): 3 slabs (12 H100-equivalent GPUs)
  * Designed to keep tail latency under p99 requirement for 70B use-cases
  * Fallback policy: when Gold exhausted, route to Silver A100 pool with model quantization and notify client with degrade message

Conversion / example math (in workbook tab "conversion_examples"):
- 1 slab = 4 physical GPUs (default mapping)
- Example monthly commit: Bronze 6 slabs + Silver 10 slabs + Gold 3 slabs = 19 slabs = 76 GPUs committed monthly
- Token/hr example (approx): embeddings pool (24 L4): 18M tokens/hr; Silver pool (40 A100): 9M tokens/hr gen; Gold (12 H100): 6M tokens/hr for 70B workloads (higher per-token compute)
- Pricing note: H100 slab ~1.55x A100 slab in committed pricing inside Redwood's Dedicated pricing bands (final pricing in workbook under tab Pricing_Scenarios)

Operational notes and SLA mechanics:
- Overage: chargeable beyond committed capacity, with automated fallback to on-demand pool (if allowed) and optional soft-throttling to preserve SLOs.
- Autoscaling guardrails: we include a burst credit system (30-minute daily bucket) and can enforce per-tenant microburst limits (configurable).
- Isolation: logical isolation via per-tenant Kubernetes namespaces + per-tenant KV caches. Physical co-tenancy will be used for Bronze and Silver; Gold recommended for isolated H100s per compliance-tier customers.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether Dataspan wants the Gold slab to be physically isolated (no shared H100s) — we can price both options in the workbook.
2) If acceptable, we'll convert the workbook into an MSA addendum draft with explicit slab definitions, SLA paragraphs, and overage terms.

Attachments: slab_commitment_workbook_20280601.xlsx (tabs: slab_definitions, conversion_examples, Pricing_Scenarios, SLA_addendum_draft)

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through the numbers.
